notes:
Summary: Marigold builds a multi-tenant escalation orchestration layer used by several enterprise contact centers. Primary interest in Redwood is improving reliability during incident bursts (seasonal peaks and large campaign-driven spikes) while keeping per-token costs inside current targets. POC goal: demonstrate 99.9% request completion under synthetic + real traffic bursts and graceful degradation to cheaper model variants when capacity constrained.

Background/context: - Current architecture: hybrid (GCP + some on-prem connectors), uses a mixture of in-house microservices to orchestrate agent assist + outbound reranking. Cache layer exists but not tuned for prefix reuse across agents. - Pain: spikes from product incidents and promotional campaigns produce long queue times and a surge of concurrent session state (KV caches explode). Attempts to autoscale increase cost rapidly and still miss SLA for tail latency.

Technical requirements and targets: - Workloads: agentAssist (real-time short chat completions), ticketSummarization (batch, post-call), toolCalling (workflow triggers: crm lookups, case-creation), reranking for suggested responses. - Latency targets: median < 120ms for agentAssist, p95 < 600ms under normal load; p95 < 1.2s acceptable in spike if fallbacks applied. - Throughput targets: baseline 1.5k concurrent agent sessions, burst up to 12k concurrent sessions for up to 30 minutes during campaigns. - Cost sensitivity: must not exceed 20% increase in monthly inference spend during expected peaks. - Model preferences: open-model family preferred; also exploring Redwood verified quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. Need model fallback matrix and metrics on quality delta.

Security/compliance items: - Must support SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and centralized audit logs to forward to Splunk. - Data residency: EU customer subsets require region pinning. - KMS integration for customer-managed keys on private deployment.

POC plan and acceptance criteria: - Phase 1 (2 weeks): basic integration with Redwood hosted API, validate agentAssist latency and tool-calling reliability in staging traffic. - Phase 2 (3 weeks): run synthetic peak simulation (traffic generator provided by Marigold + Redwood) up to 12k concurrent sessions, validate graceful fallback policy and measure cost delta. - Phase 3 (2 weeks): security review and run canary in a subset of production tenants behind VPC and SCIM. Acceptance: sustained 99.9% success rate for requests, documented fallback behavior, and <20% spend increase during controlled peak.

Recent interactions / notes from calls: - 2026-02-18 Kickoff w/ Jordan, Aisha, and Marigold CTO (ff_2026-02-18). CTO: "If we can't keep agents live during Black Friday-like spikes we lose big accounts." - 2026-03-02 Peak simulation planning; Redwood suggested model routing + prefix caching changes (ff_2026-03-02). - Security team requested SOC2/ISO artifacts and draft network diagram (drive link shared). - SE delivered initial load-test script; observed KV cache growth >4x under multi-session reuse patterns.

Quotes/paraphrases: - "We need predictable degradation, not total failure — automated fallbacks to smaller quantized models is acceptable if suggestion quality stays >85% baseline." - "Tool-calls must remain idempotent under retries; any duplication is unacceptable."

Open items / blockers: - Marigold security requires ISO27001 evidence — Redwood to provide attestation or timeline. - Commercial: need a Dedicated pricing estimate for the 12k-concurrent burst profile. - Technical: confirm that Redwood's KV cache strategy will work with Marigold's multi-tenant session keys without cross-tenant leakage.
